createdAt.description:
Every timestamp at which a concurrent write first introduced this binding. These are
unsigned display metadata: neither the earliest value nor the set's size establishes which
binding is authoritative. The UUID, key, URL, and certificate are the binding.

DatumMetadata.description:
What dmeta records about one datum slot.

`signatures` is a **current competing set**, not an append-only audit index: a write replaces
the entries it observed at its base heads with its own, and concurrent writers can leave several.
The list is the shape of that set because a signature has no identity independent of its own
bytes — keying a map on a hash of the entry would store the derivation beside its inputs. Which
entries a write replaces is decided by the repository against the heads it wrote from; this type
only holds the result. Timestamps help display history. They are not signed, and they establish
neither identity nor authorization.

uuids.description:
The aliases bound to this datum, each mapped to `true`: a set stored as a map so that
concurrent insertions merge by key. A binding is immutable once written, and the entry
carries no datum key to rebind. Concurrent creators of the datum each create this entry, so
Automerge keeps several copies and shows one; every reader unions `uuids` across all of
them rather than reading the visible copy.

Dmeta.description:
The compact provenance datum. Maps are ordered so snapshots and derived evidence are stable.

A datum's aliases live under the datum itself, in [`DatumMetadata::uuids`] (ADR 020, the dmeta
cut, item 5), so finding them is a read of that one entry rather than a scan of an index the
document grows by one binding per datum. Nothing looks a datum up by alias; a claim signs its
`(key, uuid)` pair, so an alias that also appears under another key cannot be taken for this
one. The chosen alias for a signature is the lexicographically smallest one in the union of
`uuids` across every concurrent copy of the datum's entry, as visible in the writing
transaction.

docUuids.description:
Which document each `docUuid` names. A normal branch carries its origin's changes, and with
them the origin's signature entries and this index's bindings for the origin; merging back
brings the branch's bindings along. A signature's claim names the document it was made on,
and this index is how the entry that carries no document id is tied to that claim.
